commitResults.messageBody:
Move command classification, task construction, date validation, and
task index parsing out of Milo. Keep CommandType as a simple enum so
parsing rules have one owner and Milo can focus on command
orchestration.

This preserves existing console behavior while establishing the first
standalone component toward the target OOP design.

Replace Milo's raw ArrayList with a TaskList that owns ordered task
state and exposes add, delete, mark, unmark, lookup, and snapshot
operations. Keep save-failure rollback behavior unchanged while routing
all mutations through the new boundary.

This gives future command classes a stable collaborator instead of
coupling them to Milo's internal collection.

Move file-path handling, directory creation, temporary-file cleanup,
and atomic replacement out of Milo. Inject the data path through Storage
and route all task mutations through its save method.

This preserves current persistence and rollback behavior while giving
future command classes a dedicated storage collaborator.

Move scanner ownership, welcome text, dividers, errors, task listings,
and command confirmations out of Milo. Route all user interaction
through Ui while leaving orchestration and persistence rollback
unchanged.

This gives future command classes a single presentation collaborator and
keeps the main class independent of console formatting details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks when Milo starts
commitResults.messageBody:
Teach Storage to reconstruct todos, deadlines, and events from the
existing line format, including completion states. Convert Milo into an
instance coordinator that initializes its TaskList from Storage and
falls back to an empty list after loading errors.

Extend the ordered UI suite with a real restart scenario and cleanup so
persisted state is verified without contaminating later cases.

Move the app coordinator to milo and group parsing, storage, tasks,
UI, and exceptions into responsibility-based subpackages. Add explicit
imports so src/main/java remains the source root and update launch and
test references to the fully qualified entry point.

This establishes stable namespace boundaries for the command hierarchy
without changing console behavior.

Add an abstract Command API and concrete add, delete, exit, list,
mark, and unmark implementations. Move task mutation, persistence
rollback, and result presentation from Milo into those command classes.

Make Parser construct executable commands so Milo can run them without
knowing individual command types. This completes the A-MoreOOP stretch
design while preserving console behavior.

Add the Gradle wrapper and configure Java 25, JUnit, application, and
Shadow JAR support from the add-gradle-support branch.

Point the application plugin at milo.Milo so Gradle run and the generated
duke.jar launch the current packaged entry point.

Add comprehensive coverage for TaskList construction, insertion,
deletion, retrieval, status changes, sizing, snapshots, and clearing.

Exercise valid positions, boundary failures, ordering, idempotence,
defensive copying, and immutable snapshots so regressions in task-list
state management are caught by Gradle.

Declare Milo's packaged entry point explicitly in the Shadow JAR
manifest so the generated duke.jar can be launched with java -jar.

Document the wrapper commands, artifact location, launch command, and
runtime data path for Windows and Unix-like systems.

Add JavaDoc coverage for exposed constructors, enum constants,
protected state, return values, and command validation contracts.

Complete the generated API documentation without warnings so every
public or protected class and method has a usable description.

commitResults.messageTitle: Conform source to Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Indent switch cases and wrapped expressions consistently, and mark
intentional switch fallthrough explicitly.

Align JavaDoc tags and add their required punctuation so the source
follows the project-wide SE-EDU conventions.

Parse find commands into a dedicated command and keep filtering within
the task model while the UI owns result presentation.

Match descriptions without regard to letter case, preserve task order,
and reject missing keywords without modifying or saving the task list.
Add focused JUnit and console regression coverage for the new behavior.

Integrate complete API documentation and warning-free JavaDoc
generation from the parallel JavaDoc branch.

Integrate SE-EDU formatting, switch fallthrough markers, and JavaDoc
punctuation from the parallel coding-standard branch.

Resolve overlapping Deadline and Event documentation by retaining the
new API descriptions while applying the corrected style.

Integrate case-insensitive keyword search through a dedicated command,
task-model filtering, and numbered UI results.

Resolve CommandType, Parser, and TaskList conflicts by preserving the
JavaDoc and coding-standard improvements alongside the new find flow.
Include focused JUnit tests and full console regression coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align repository setup with the Milo project
commitResults.messageBody:
Record the Java, Git, Markdown, and required UI testing conventions
used for future project changes, and ignore local agent tooling.

Remove the obsolete Duke banner entry point now that milo.Milo is the
configured application and executable JAR main class.
Add an FXML chat window that routes user input through Milo's existing command logic. Keep the console entry point available for regression testing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task statistics and preserve state on save errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need an overview of their current tasks without counting each
entry manually. Add stats to report totals, completion percentage, and
counts by task type without changing saved data.

Use the same English date format for display and storage so September
tasks survive a restart. Retry transient access-denied replacements on
Windows with a bounded delay, preserve the original completion state
when saving fails, and announce success only after persistence succeeds.

Add statistics, retry, and rollback regression tests and update the
user guide and console test plan. Isolate response-test storage so
repeated test runs remain independent.

Validation: 46 JUnit tests, 16 console UI cases, and 1,000 save/reload
cycles passed with Java 25. Rebuild the JavaFX executable JAR.

Make internal contracts visible at the parser, task-index conversion,
and storage-status boundaries so programming errors are caught when
assertions are enabled. Keep user input validation exception-based.

Check that parser input is trimmed and non-null, validated task numbers
map to existing indices, and stored status symbols match the format.

Validation: all 14 console UI cases passed on Java 25 with assertions
enabled.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task parsing and isolate response tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Parsing all task types in one method makes each format harder to
follow. Dispatch to small todo, deadline, and event parsing methods
while retaining the existing command behavior and error messages.

Give each response test a temporary storage directory so earlier runs
cannot leave tasks that change later assertions.

Validation: all 14 console UI cases passed on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Map stored task lines with a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading performs a one-to-one conversion from saved lines to tasks.
Express that conversion as an ordered stream mapping instead of a
loop that manually builds the result list.

TaskList already takes a defensive mutable copy of loaded tasks, so
the stream's immutable result remains compatible with task operations.

Validation: all 14 console UI cases passed on Java 25, including
persistence and task changes after loading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run Java 25 checks on Windows and Linux
commitResults.messageBody:
Local testing alone does not verify every pushed change consistently
across supported operating systems. Add GitHub Actions jobs that run
JUnit checks and build the executable JAR on pushes and pull requests.

Use Java 25 and each platform's native Gradle wrapper, with read-only
repository permissions. Document the equivalent local check command.

Validation: the Gradle checks and JAR build passed locally. Hosted
Windows and Linux runs will execute after this workflow is pushed.
Add assertions for internal task contracts
